title: US Visa Curbs Push Indian IT Firms Toward Offshore Hiring, Analysts Say
excerpt: Washington has frozen green card sponsorship at eight major employers and attached a $100,000 payment to many new H-1B hires from abroad, and analysts say the industry's response is to move the job to India rather than the worker to America.
body:
• On October 8, the US Labor Department suspended eight employers — Microsoft, Adobe, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant and Capgemini — from PERM, the first step in employer-sponsored green cards, accepting no new applications and processing no pending ones.
  • Separately, USCIS says H-1B petitions filed at or after 12:01 a.m. Eastern on September 21, 2025 for workers outside the US without a valid H-1B visa must be accompanied by a $100,000 payment, paid by the employer via pay.gov before filing.
  • The PERM freeze does not cancel existing H-1B visas or ban H-1B hiring, GTRI says — but analysts say the combined curbs push firms to expand delivery from India instead of relocating staff.
  • If you work for one of the eight firms and were counting on a sponsored green card, your PERM case is frozen with no end date announced — check your status with your employer now rather than assuming your queue position is moving.

Washington has made the route to the US slower and costlier for Indian engineers — and the industry's answer, analysts say, is to move the job rather than the worker: as visas tighten, more of the work is done from India.

Who is affected — exactly

Two different groups are affected, by two different measures. The first is employees of the eight named firms who need PERM — the Permanent Labor Certification Program, in which an employer certifies no qualified American is available for the job — to move toward a green card. The second is prospective H-1B hires outside the United States, whose petitions carry the $100,000 payment described below. Existing H-1B visas are not cancelled by either measure, and workers in the US granted a change of status, amendment or extension are outside the $100,000 payment under USCIS guidance. Amazon, Google, Meta, Apple and other large H-1B employers not on the PERM list are not covered by the suspension, GTRI noted.

What changed, precisely

The PERM suspension was announced on October 8 by Vice President JD Vance and Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling, citing alleged visa fraud, according to IPA News Pack's analysis. Microsoft president Brad Smith has rejected the allegations, IPA reported. The department will neither accept new PERM applications from the eight firms nor process pending ones.

The H-1B payment is separate. Under the presidential proclamation of September 19, 2025, certain petitions filed at or after 12:01 a.m. Eastern on September 21, 2025 must be accompanied by an additional $100,000 payment as a condition of eligibility, USCIS states on its H-1B Specialty Occupations page. It applies to beneficiaries outside the US without a valid H-1B visa, and to petitions requesting consular or port-of-entry notification. It does not apply to previously issued, currently valid H-1B visas or to petitions filed before the cutoff. Payment must be made through pay.gov before filing, and petitions subject to the payment that are filed without proof of payment or a Homeland Security exception will be denied, USCIS says. Exceptions are described by USCIS as extraordinarily rare.

A third measure is only a proposal: an additional $103,265 fee on every cap-subject H-1B petition, projecting about $8.8 billion a year, IPA reported. It is not yet in effect; the next cap season begins in spring 2027.

Why analysts expect more offshore hiring

The offshore shift was already under way. The National Foundation for American Policy found the top seven Indian IT firms won just 4,573 new H-1B approvals in fiscal 2025, 37 percent fewer than the year before and 70 percent below fiscal 2015, IPA reported. GTRI founder Ajay Srivastava said 91.7 percent of India's software and IT-enabled services exports were delivered from India in 2025-26, against 8.3 percent by professionals at overseas client locations, and that Indian professionals account for over 70 percent of approved H-1B petitions annually, according to People Matters' report of GTRI's assessment. The US accounted for $119.7 billion, or 54.1 percent, of India's $221.4 billion in such exports, GTRI said.

Analysts argue the new costs accelerate that pattern. A Mint explainer concluded the higher fees will force companies to expand offshore delivery rather than relocate talent, prioritising senior, high-wage talent for US placements while shifting entry and mid-level roles offshore, Mint reported. GTRI likewise said the freeze could encourage growth in India's global capability centres if retaining talent in the US becomes harder. These are analyst expectations, not announced company decisions — no firm cited in the reporting has announced an offshore shift in response to the October suspension.

What to do next — and what happens if you do nothing

If your employer is one of the eight suspended firms and your sponsorship was at the PERM stage, ask your employer or immigration counsel in writing whether your case is frozen and what alternatives they are assessing. If you are being hired from outside the US on an H-1B, the $100,000 payment is your employer's obligation, payable before filing — confirm it has been handled, because USCIS says a covered petition filed without proof of payment will be denied. Watch whether the proposed $103,265 cap-subject fee is finalised before the spring 2027 cap season. Doing nothing carries a specific cost for the PERM group: IPA noted that an engineer mid-queue at an affected firm now waits with no end date, and the Labor Department has published no written notice setting a duration.
